paper.title_en: Information-Induced Shielding in Open Quantum Systems: A Bidirectional Perspective on Type-2 Epistemic Uncertainty and Entropy Dynamics
paper.abstract_en: We describe a self-shielding mechanism in open quantum systems by coupling Lindblad dynamics with an interval Type-2 fuzzy observer model. To avoid conceptual ambiguities associated with physical measurement apparatuses, we model the environment as an information-theoretic agent characterized by bounded cognitive resolution. We identify a stability regime characterized by a stable steady state. By formulating the mathematical expansion of the footprint of uncertainty (FOU), our comparative dynamics reveal that as the system's back-action strength (k) increases, the observer's reduced resolution significantly suppresses both the effective decoherence rate and the growth of Von Neumann entropy. This protective phase is evaluated through extensive stochastic simulations ($N=1000$) and continuous crossover mapping, offering a theoretical framework for understanding the quantum-to-classical transition in complex, high-noise environments.
